clue.text: It's one of my 14s, but did I perceive something of the others?

definitions.text: It's one of my 14s, but did I perceive something of the others?

parts.words: It's one of my 14s, but did I perceive something of the others?
parts.note: the setter's question about a car (the Toyota of 2) and a cat (the felines of 9/4), phrased as a sentence reading the same both ways

explanation.walkthrough: The other themed entries are about a car and cats, so the solver asks whether they saw one or the other; the sentence asking it reads identically from either end, as 14 requires.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous symmetrical sentence asking whether a vehicle or a feline was glimpsed, matching the theme of the other long entries.

clue.text: 14 — Japanese model is what it is?

definitions.text: 14 — Japanese model is what it is?

parts.words: 14 — Japanese model is what it is?
parts.note: a tautology about a Japanese car make, saying the model is simply itself, in a sentence reading the same both ways

explanation.walkthrough: 14 is the theme word: a sequence of letters reading the same backwards. The saying 'X is X' applied to a Japanese car maker happens to be symmetrical letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tautological phrase about a Japanese vehicle brand that reads identically backwards, so it is an example of the theme.

clue.text: Saint Paul's man, perhaps, finding one with Saint Martin extremely unreliable

indicators.note: something unreliable cannot be trusted to stay in shape, so the letters are thrown into a new order
extremely points to the extreme ends of the word Martin, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone from a cathedral finds a fellow called Saint Martin highly untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint Paul looks like the apostle or the London cathedral, but it is the capital of Minnesota. Shuffle ONE, SAINT and MN (the ends of Martin, picked by 'extremely') under 'unreliable'.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul is the state capital of Minnesota, so a man living there is a native of that US state.

clue.text: See 9
Two articles taken from a Volkswagen, over here!

indicators.note: taken from says the two named pieces are removed from the car model

parts.note: the Passat is a Volkswagen car model
A is the indefinite article, here taken twice

explanation.surface: Two items have been stolen from someone's Volkswagen, and a witness calls for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two articles' sounds like belongings lifted from the car; they are the letter A twice, taken out of PASSAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection used to catch someone's attention quietly, much like a whispered call to come over.

clue.text: One of two is introduced to popular water sport, making one distinctive

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: introduced to says the first group of pieces is put inside the word for the water sport

parts.note: diving is a water sport
I is the Roman numeral for one
dual means of or consisting of two
taken as written

explanation.surface: One of a pair is introduced to a fashionable water sport, which makes them stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: To individualise something is to give it a distinct character of its own, setting it apart from others.

clue.text: Drink containing Irish water servant's left for traditional food

indicators.note: containing says the drink holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink
a lough is an Irish lake or sea inlet
a man is an old word for a manservant; the possessive gives MAN'S

explanation.surface: A bowl of drink holds some Irish water, and the servant has left to fetch traditional food.
explanation.walkthrough: A ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: This cold plate of bread, cheese and pickle is served as classic English pub fare.

clue.text: Abundance of crystals treating ailments

indicators.note: treating suggests processing or working on the word ailments, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A large supply of healing crystals is being used to treat illnesses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests crystal healing; the crystals are actually salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine for rock salt is a rich source of crystals, and the phrase means a plentiful supply.

clue.text: 14 for weak old lions, perhaps?

parts.note: a description of aged, frail big cats, given in a phrase reading the same both ways as 14 requires

explanation.walkthrough: Lions are big cats, and weak old ones are doddery cats; the phrase describing them reads identically backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning doddering cats, which also reads identically from the right as from the left.

clue.text: Mother leaves African country via an African native

indicators.note: leaves says the word for mother departs from the country's name

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
ma is a familiar word for mother
by means via, as in travel by road
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother departs an African country by way of a local person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African country' invites the answer itself, but it is Mali, losing MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in Libya, a North African country, is a native of that place.

clue.text: Urgent: couple of Latins getting frisky in clandestine love affair

indicators.note: getting frisky suggests lively, playful movement, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals, the Latin way of writing a couple

explanation.surface: An urgent message: two Latin lovers are getting amorous in a secret affair.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrigue is a secret romantic liaison, an older sense of the word alongside plotting.

clue.text: See 19
Recall wee teddy's head cuddled by minor, producing comforting words

indicators.note: cuddled by says the pieces are held inside the word for minor

parts.note: slight means minor or small

indicators.note: recall suggests calling back, so the word for wee is read in reverse

parts.note: pee is a word for wee, urine

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A small child remembers wetting the bed while hugging a teddy, and hears soothing words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' looks like the Scottish word for small, but here it is urine; 'Recall' reads it backwards, and 'head' takes the first letter of teddy's.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedtime wish said to children going to bed, meant to reassure them as they drift off.

clue.text: One is drawn onward

parts.note: the phrase drawn onward is itself an example, reading the same letter by letter from either end

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone pulled forward; in fact 'drawn onward' spelt backwards is 'drawn onward' again, so it is an instance of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase that reads the same backwards and forwards, as 'drawn onward' does.

clue.text: Ride through change in Oxford or Cambridge, possibly?

indicators.note: through says one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: vary means change
to sit a horse is to ride it

explanation.surface: A horse ride through changing scenery in one of England's old university towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Varsity is a British informal word for a university, used especially of Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Varsity is an old informal term for a university, so either of the ancient English universities is one.

clue.text: Describing lung membranes, soft with questionable allure

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: questionable suggests something doubtful or out of order, so the letters of allure are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes the lining of the lungs, soft and of doubtful charm.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleura are the membranes lining the lungs and chest cavity; the adjective describes them.

clue.text: Fib about alcoholic drink being one that's non-alcoholic?

indicators.note: about says the word for fib goes round the drink

parts.note: a lie is a fib
mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey

explanation.surface: Someone fibs about an alcoholic drink that is actually alcohol-free.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition contradicts the alcoholic drink inside the wordplay, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Limeade is a soft drink of lime juice and sweetened water, served without alcohol.

clue.text: Strain, say, behind party rivalry

indicators.note: behind says the piece for strain comes after the piece for party

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a political party

indicators.note: say signals that the word for strain is heard, not spelt

parts.note: tension means strain

explanation.surface: Stress, for example, is behind the rivalry within a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Contention is competition or dispute between opponents, a struggle for the same thing.

clue.text: Start lap dancing, showing tail?

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A lap dancer starts the act by showing off a rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lap dancing' reads as one phrase; 'lap' is fodder and 'dancing' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail of something is its end or final section.

clue.text: Elegant, idly swimming in water

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit inside the word for water

parts.note: a lake is a body of water

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters floating about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone swims lazily and gracefully in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladylike means refined and graceful in manner, as an elegant woman was expected to be.

clue.text: See 1
Deliver key to open road in Paris

indicators.note: to open says the key goes into the road word, opening it up

parts.note: rue is French for street
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A key is handed over to open up a street in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a door key; it is the computer escape key, ESC.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to deliver them from danger, setting them free.

clue.text: Endless siren in sacred chant

indicators.note: endless says the last letter of the word for siren is dropped

parts.note: a seductive woman is sometimes called a mantrap

explanation.surface: A singing siren repeats a holy chant without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'siren' looks like the mythical singer or an alarm, but it is a temptress, a mantrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred word or phrase repeated in meditation or prayer, especially in Hinduism and Buddhism.

clue.text: A fish going backwards around little island in the Caribbean

indicators.note: around says the reversed pair surrounds the word for little
going backwards says the article and the fish word are read in reverse

parts.note: cod is a fish
mini means little

explanation.surface: A fish swims backwards around a small island in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going backwards' turns the whole pair, giving DOCA, which then wraps the word for little; 'little' sounds like it describes the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominica is an island nation in the Lesser Antilles of the eastern Caribbean.
